acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: The Rockefeller Foundation transferred Gordon Conway's President's Office files to the Rockefeller Archive Center in 2005. A deposit agreement between the Rockefeller Foundation and the RAC, June 7, 2022, formalized the terms of the deposit of RF records.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Gordon Conway's President's Office files are arranged into nine series:

1) Board of Trustees 2) Administration, Management, Strategy and Planning 3) Program Activities and Themes 4) Regional Offices 5) Foundations, Agricultural Institutes, Universities, and Other 6) Organizations (A-Z) 7) People 8) Rockefeller Family and Philanthropies 9) Speeches, Papers, Publications

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: SG 21.3 documents Gordon Conway's tenure as president of the Rockefeller Foundation from 1998-2004. The records reflect Conway's influence on the RF's program directions, administration, and culture. Embracing the RF's mission to "promote the well-being of humanity throughout the world," Conway focused the RF's programs directly on improving the lives and livelihoods of the poor and excluded and on ensuring that globalization worked for all and that everyone share in its benefits.

The files consist mainly of email correspondence, notes, and memos between Conway, his senior staff, and program officers, as well as correspondence with trustees and the board, and with outside colleagues and organizations. The internal correspondence highlights the significant roles and input of RF officers and staff in implementing policy and programs.

An agricultural ecologist by training, Conway called for a second or "doubly green" revolution, that would take into account environmental issues, local constraints, and local knowledge and inputs. Early in his tenure, RF programs were regrouped under the themes of Creativity and Culture, Food Security, Health Equity, and Working Communities, plus a cross-cutting theme of Global Inclusion, which fostered connections between these programs.

As president of the RF, Conway also served as a public voice. He was a frequent speaker and contributor on issues of Food Security, Health Equity, globalization and equitable development, etc. He spoke at agricultural conferences, workshops, UN panels, universities, and government hearings, often on themes of Food for All in Africa or Asia, the Two Faces of Globalization, and the Risks and Promises of Biotechnology. Notably, Conway addressed the Monsanto Corporation in private, and subsequently in print, on its responsibilities to the developing world.

The importance of partnership for achieving goals of equity and inclusion is another theme documented in these files. Significant collaborative ventures include the African Agricultural Technology Foundation, the Foundation Partnership for Strengthening African Universities, the Public Intellectual Property Resource for Agriculture (PIPRA), the Foundation Executives Group (FEG), the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative, the Mother to Child Transmission Plus Initiative, etc.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 1 documents interactions between the RF president and officers and the Board of Trustees, concerning board and staff appointments, program strategy, policy, and general governance. The files contain correspondence, memos, presentations, and notes on meetings, board discussions, and other topics. The series does not contain board books or other formal documentation of the board's activities. Rather, it shows the RF staff's preparations for board presentations, as well as mutual efforts to foster dialogue and understanding between the board and foundation staff. The series also includes files on the various board committees and on individual trustees.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 2 contains general files for Gordon Conway, his Vice Presidents Lincoln Chen and Robert Herdt, and other officers and administrative departments. The series notably documents Conway's reshaping of the RF's program and culture. It includes Gordon Conway's notes, presentations, a vision paper for the Next Five Years, and files on the strategic planning process the RF undertook in 1999-2001. The series also includes records of Senior Management Team meetings, 1999-2004; staff retreats, retirements, and other events; RF responses to 9/11 and its aftermath; and responses to hearings on nonprofit governance.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The folder for January-June 2001 (box 13, folder 102), includes Gordon Conway's agendas for the weeks of January 5, March 29, April 3, and April 11, 2001. The agendas list pending items and describe context and actions to be taken. They presumably served as a checklist for Conway's assistant, April Chapman, in her conversations with him. While the agendas include some references to the Senior Management Team, they do not pertain directly to it. While informative, the agendas appear to be routine documents that were inadvertently left in the file.

scopecontent.p: Series 3 documents projects the RF supported in partnership with other foundations, governments, NGOs, and the private sector, focused on expanding access to information and technology, building local capacity, fostering investment that benefits the poor, meeting the Millennium Development Goals, etc.

The series also contains program files for the RF's work under its four main program themes - Creativity and Culture, Food Security, Health Equity, and Working Communities – and its cross-theme of Global Inclusion. The files, which are sometimes uneven, include correspondence with program officers, meeting records, and other materials. The program files are arranged by year and then by program area or theme. The series also includes records of Gordon Conway's visits to Africa in October-November 1998, as well as of some later trips.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: As its title indicates, Series 5 contains records relating to Foundations, Agricultural Institutes, and Universities, as well as records on the UK Government and records relating to some United Nations programs (and Gordon Conway's involvement with them). The series includes records on the Foundation Executives Group (FEG), 1999-2003, an association of foundation heads who met annually to discuss common interests. Agricultural files include the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR) and its various member organizations. This series also includes files relating to Conway's meetings with Monsanto and his June 1999 address to the Monsanto board, in which he warned of the consequences of its sterile seed ("Terminator") technology for farmers in the developing world and for its own reputation. Conway frequently spoke at conferences, meetings, or other gatherings, several of which addresses are documented in this series.
